story.title: Senate Approves Bipartisan Sanctions Bill Targeting Russia and Iran
story.summary: The Senate has passed a bipartisan sanctions bill aimed at Russia and Iran, named after the late Senator Lindsey Graham. The legislation, which received overwhelming support with a vote of 86-11, seeks to penalize countries that continue to purchase Russian oil and gas, aiming to reduce revenue for the Russian government amid ongoing conflicts.

timeline_highlights.title: US Senate Approves Comprehensive Sanctions Bill Against Russian Energy Sector
timeline_highlights.summary: The US Senate has approved a comprehensive sanctions package aimed at targeting Russia's energy revenues. The legislation includes sanctions on Russian officials, oligarchs, and financial institutions, as well as measures against the shadow fleet used to circumvent restrictions on oil exports. Additionally, it grants the President the authority to impose tariffs of up to 500% on Russian imports, including gas and oil.
key_facts: Sanctions target Russian energy revenues and officials.
Includes measures against financial institutions and shadow fleet.
President can impose tariffs up to 500% on Russian imports.

related_stories.title: Court Halts Trump's White House Ballroom Construction, Appeals Expected
related_stories.summary: A federal appeals court has ordered the halt of construction on Donald Trump's planned $400 million ballroom at the White House, stating that such a significant alteration requires congressional approval. The ruling follows a challenge from the National Trust for Historic Preservation and is seen as a test of presidential power. Trump has announced plans to appeal the decision to the Supreme Court.

related_stories.summary: Abelardo de la Espriella has been sworn in as the president of Colombia, vowing to launch an 'all-out war' on narco-terrorism and crack down on armed drug gangs. The United States has pledged $1 billion in support to Colombia following his inauguration.

related_stories.title: Senate Confirms Todd Blanche as Attorney General in Narrow Vote
related_stories.summary: The U.S. Senate confirmed Todd Blanche as Attorney General with a narrow 50-49 vote early Saturday morning. Blanche, a former personal lawyer for President Trump, received crucial support from Republican Senator Bill Cassidy, who was the deciding vote in a contentious confirmation process. Concerns regarding the independence of the office were raised during the proceedings.
